metadata.title: Charak Samhita - Complete Chapter Data
metadata.description: Comprehensive structured data of all 120 chapters from Charak Samhita with key concepts, topics, and summaries

keyConcepts: Tridosha (Vata, Pitta, Kapha) - three bodily doshas
Medical ethics and qualities of physician
Six tastes (Rasa) and their effects on dosha
chapters.summary: The first chapter establishes foundational concepts of Ayurveda including the definition of life (Ayu), the three doshas, six principles of knowledge, and the theory of similarity/dissimilarity. It describes the origin of Ayurvedic knowledge from Brahma through Indra toBharadwaja and then to Atreya's disciples. Includes detailed classification of drugs, herbs, salts, urine therapies, and milk varieties. Emphasizes the importance of complete knowledge of medicines and ethical medical practice.
Describes various herbs and medicines used during and after Panchakarma (bio-purification) procedures. Covers emetic and purgative drugs, their preparations, and indications.
Describes topical medications and external applications including pastes, poultices, and medicated oils for various diseases.
Provides details of fifty Mahakashaya (groups of ten medicines) and six hundred evacuatives to be used in various diseases.

chapters.englishName: Proper Quantity of Food and Daily Regimen
chapters.summary: Describes proper quantity of food based on digestive power (Agni), heavy and light to digest foods, and daily health maintenance procedures including massage, nasal therapy, eye care, oral hygiene, and personal care.

keyConcepts: Diet and lifestyle modifications by season
Dosha accumulation and alleviation by season
chapters.summary: Explains modifications in diet and lifestyle according to six seasons (Ritu) to maintain health and prevent seasonal diseases.

keyConcepts: Diseases due to suppression of urges
chapters.summary: Explains importance of suppressible and non-suppressible natural urges, diseases caused by their suppression, and their management.
Describes Sadvritta (general code of conduct) for maintaining health and healthy relations with society.

keyConcepts: Four aspects: Vaidya, Dravya, Upasthata, Rogi
chapters.summary: Describes four aspects of therapeutics - physician, medicine, patient, and caretaker with their essential qualities.
Explains classification of diseases based on prognosis and emphasizes thorough diagnosis before initiating treatment.
Deals with three types of desires, strength, causes of diseases, their types, pathways, physicians, and therapies.
Describes good and bad qualities/functions of Vata, Pitta, and Kapha doshas.

keyConcepts: Types of sneha (ghee, oil, fat, marrow)
chapters.summary: Provides guidelines for proper use of sneha (lipids) for Shodhana (purification) or Shamana (pacification) purposes.
Explains various types of swedana (fomentation) recommended for various diseases as preparation for purification.
Emphasizes how a physician should be well equipped before administering Shodhana procedures. Provides outline for hospital and standard procedures.
Depicts importance of Shodhana over Shamana therapy, details of properly/improperly administered procedures, and theory of natural destruction.
Provides details of diseases like shiroroga, hridroga, eighteen types of kshaya, vidradhi, and madhumeha.
Elucidates various types of edema and their classification.

keyConcepts: Forty-eight diseases caused by dosha combination
chapters.summary: Reveals types of about 48 diseases caused by combination of doshas.
Dedicated to diseases caused by single dosha - Vata, Pitta, or Kapha.
Describes eight types of marginalized people with clinical significance, focusing on obesity and emaciation.
Describes six types of treatment - Langhana, Brimhana, Snehana, Swedana, Rukshana, and Stambhana.
Deals with diseases caused due to over-nourishment or under-nourishment along with their treatment.
Deals with diseases not cured by above-mentioned therapies and diseases due to vitiation of rakta (blood).
Brings forth perspective of origin of human beings and diseases. Describes 155 Agrya entities.
Describes Ayurvedic pharmacology - rasa, veerya, vipaka, prabhava, and concept of incompatible diet.
Provides details of Ayurvedic dietetics, wide variety of food and beverages with medicinal values.

keyConcepts: Formation of body tissues from diet
chapters.summary: Deals with formation of body tissues from diet, immunity, diseases originated from various dhatus, and dosha migration.
Deals with ten locations in human body where Prana resides, attributes of life-saving and disease-causing physicians.
Deals with importance of heart, ten major blood vessels, definition of life, and aim of Ayurvedic science.
Introduces basic principles of diagnosis and disease fever with involvement of rasa dhatu as dushya. Discusses disorders of hyper-pyrexia and various types of fever.
Deals with various pathologies related to rakta dhatu. Details diagnosis of bleeding disorders.
Deals with mamsa dhatu predominantly. Describes diagnosis of lumps in abdomen and tumors.
Involves meda dhatu predominantly. Describes diagnosis of disorders of lipid metabolism including diabetes.
Involves seven dushya. Deals with diagnosis of skin disorders including leprosy and other skin conditions.
Deals with pathology of emaciation. Describes diagnosis of degenerative disorders involving depletion of body tissues.
Explains insanity and psychotic disorders. Covers diagnosis of mental health conditions.
Deals with epilepsy and seizure disorders. Describes diagnosis and classification of epileptic conditions.

keyConcepts: Role of rasa in dosha vitiation
chapters.summary: Explains role of rasa, ghee, oil, and honey in dosha vitiation and pacification. Describes eight specific factors for food processing.
Further guides dietary regulations and consequences if not followed properly. Describes disorders due to ama.
Deals with prevention of epidemic disorders caused by polluted environment. Covers social hygiene aspects.
Explains three ways to acquire knowledge of diseases based on authority, perception, and reasoning.
Deals with detailed description of srotas (transportation channels) in the body, their roots, and vitiation signs.
Details five categories of diseases based on prognosis, severity, origin, and site of origin.
Describes how patient presentation can mislead physician. Covers krmi (microorganisms) and their management.
Deals with how medical student can achieve comprehensive knowledge. Explains selection of treatise, teacher, and patient examination.

sthanas.name: Sharira Sthana
sthanas.english: Section on Human Being and Genesis

chapters.summary: Describes evolution of body from imperceptible entities to association of mind, sense organs, consciousness. Unique concepts of living vs non-living.
Micro composition of basic units of reproduction and their role in formation of healthy offspring.
Extended part of second chapter. Deals with factors causing congenital deformities and their prevention.
Dedicated to month-wise fetal development. Interesting fact about intellect during 6th month. Describes psychological development.
Whatever is in universe is represented in a person. Provides tips for mental health and cognitive functions.
Deals with knowledge of human body, definition, equilibrium for health, lifestyle, diet for maintenance.
Anthropometry is core subject. Counts number of body organs/parts and their measurements.
Overview of process for better progeny. Details monthly regimen for pregnant, delivery, postpartum care, neonatal care.
Signs and symptoms of imminent death perceived by specific changes in color (Varna).
Signs of imminent death through changes in voice (Swara).
Prognosis based on touch (Sparsha) and skin examination.
Multiple sense organ assessments for prognosis.
Clinically useful early warning signs (Purvarupa) for various conditions.
Physical signs (Bahyakarana) for death prediction.
Prognosis based on complexion (Chhaya) and radiance (Prabha).
Signs in neck region indicating death or survival.
Prognostic signs related to smell (Gandha) and causal factors.
Signs indicating immediate/sudden death.
Signs of less immediate death and gradual prognosis.
Miscellaneous prognostic signs including dreams, messengers, and occult indicators.
Describes measures that promote physical and mental health and provide general immunity. Prevents and retards aging, promotes longevity.
Deals with enhancing sexual health in healthy persons, leading to healthy progeny. Principles of aphrodisiac medicines.
Management of fever - acute and chronic, continuous, intermittent, malarial, with or without ama. Includes therapeutic measures for various fever types.
Management of bleeding disorders - two types i.e. bleeding from upper and lower channels.
Describes protuberance of abdomen - local and generalized. Local lumps termed gulma with five types.
Urinary diseases with excessive urine. Twenty types including madhumeha (diabetes mellitus). Principles of treatment for disorders due to impaired fat metabolism.
Management of eighteen types of Kushtha (skin diseases including leprosy). Chronic non-purulent bacterial, fungal and allergic skin disorders.
Rajayakshma (Syndrome like Tuberculosis). Classified into four types with detailed treatment. Treatment of various diseases due to impaired immunity.
Management of insanity and various psychotic disorders. Part of Bhuta-vidya (psychiatric disorders).
Management of epilepsy, seizures and memory disorders. Psychiatric disorder management.
Management of conditions due to activities beyond one's strength leading to chest injuries, bleeding and cachexia.
Three groups of diseases with swelling, edema and inflammation at various sites.
Conditions leading to generalized enlargement of abdomen - ascites, hepatomegaly and splenomegaly.
Types of hemorrhoids and warts along with their treatment. Medical management of haemorrhoids.
Elaborates physiological principles of Agni at various levels. Various processes of digestion and metabolism. Comprehensive management of GI disorders.
Two diseases caused mainly by vitiation of rakta - pandu roga (anemia) and kamala (jaundice). Management of hematological disorders.
Disorders of respiratory system. Clinical presentations and management of five types of hiccups and dyspnoea.
Cough of various origin and its management.
Management of various types of diarrhea and irritable bowel syndrome.
Management of Vomiting due to various somatic and psychological origin.
Types of acute inflammatory dermatological conditions such as erysipelas.
Conditions manifested in form of excessive thirst.
Management of acute and slow poisoning relating with agada-tantra (toxicology).
Management of various acute and chronic stages of alcoholic intoxication and its complications.
Wound management and surgical procedures (shalya).
Disorders due to obstruction to free movement of Vata. Disorders of three vital organs - heart, brain, kidney. Brief description of hair, ear, nose, throat and eye diseases.
Disorders of spinal-neuro-muscular degeneration in thigh and hip joint.

Vata dosha is key initiating factor for all physiological and psychological mechanisms. Disorders of digestive, nervous, musculo-skeletal systems. Extensive coverage of neurological conditions including paralysis, sciatica, etc.
Disorders due to vitiation of Vata dosha and rakta dhatu. Conditions involving deformities in small joints and vascular system.
Disorders related to male and female reproductive system, infertility and gynecological disorders. Diseases in children mentioned. Principles of time of administration and dose.
First chapter of Kalpa Sthana. Describes Madanaphala - main emetic drug with 133 recipes for therapeutic emesis.
Second emetic drug Jimutaka with 39 recipes.
Third emetic drug Ikshvaku with 45 recipes. Leaf, fruit, seed used.
Fourth emetic drug Dhamargava with 60 recipes. Fruit, flower, tender leaves used.
Fifth emetic drug Vatsaka with 18 recipes. Kutaja plant used.
Sixth emetic drug Kritavedhana with 60 recipes.
First purgative drug Shyama-Trivrita with 110 recipes. Root used.
Purgative drug Aragwadha with 12 recipes. Fruit used.
Purgative drug Tilvaka with 16 recipes. Root and bark used.
Purgative drug Sudha with 20 recipes. Milky latex used.
Purgative drug Saptala-Shankhini with 36 recipes.
Last chapter with Danti-Dravanti (49 recipes). Includes process for purification to reduce toxicity.
Gives brief overall content of all Panchakarma procedures. Highlights optimal indicators of each procedure and importance of judicious selection.
Describes Panchakarma procedures with contraindications and indications for suitable patients.
Explains procedure of Basti in detail - decoction enema (Niruha) and oil enema (Anuvasana).
Complications of unctuous enema and their management.
Instrumental defects in Basti administration and related complications.
Complications of therapeutic emesis (Vamana) and purgation (Virechana) with management.
Complications associated with decoction enema (Basti) procedure.
Enlists number of special Basti formulations with specific actions like virility enhancers, complexion promoters, etc. Also details diarrhea management.
Highlights clinician's concern over three vital organs (Basti-urinary bladder/kidneys, Hridayam-heart, Shiras-head). Describes medicated enema for protection of Marma.
Enlists special enema recipes indicated as per dosha predominance and specific clinical situations.
Details various fruits useful for enema. Includes discussion on enema therapy for animals.
Highlights excellent enema recipes superior in efficacy. Details Yapana Basti and eight factors to avoid during Panchakarma.
